newsitem.title: USA: Dow downturn may signal end to New Year rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow downturn may signal end to New Year rally.

text.p: A sharp reversal in U.S. stocks on Thursday on record volume could be a signal the market's New Year's rally is losing steam.
While a big short-term pullback may not be in the works, the rally on Wall Street may be cooling as the flood of start-of-the-year investor cash begins to slow, analysts said.

"The year-end rally may be over," said Robert Robbins, market strategist at Robinson-Humprhey Co. "We may be going into a trading range and be in a trading range for some number of weeks or at least days."
The Dow ended Thursday off 94 points, or 1.4 percent, at 6756 on record volume of 683.8 million shares. The Dow fell 151 points from its session high at 6907.
The blue chip gauge had been up over six percent in January through Wednesday.
"We've been up for so long, it wouldn't surprise me at all if we got a little further setback," said Robert von Pentz, a managing partner at Columbia Partners.
But he added that after the strong gains, a 94-point drop was not a major concern in itself.
Analysts said they would be looking at whether investors used Thursday's selloff as a buying opportunity or step to the sidelines.

Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management, noted that Wall Street was in the middle of its fourth-quarter earnings reporting season. A batch of disappointing earnings could "exacerbate" the downturn, he said.

Thus far, corporate profits have been generally on target. But lofty stock prices have led investors to give extra scrutiny to earnings reports, looking beyond the earnings per share numbers for balance-sheet details or business projections, analysts said.

One key example was market heavyweight International Business Machines Corp, which late on Tuesday reported earnings of $2.0 billion, or $3.93 a share for the quarter, ahead of the Wall Street consensus estimate of $3.88.
But analysts said the results were tainted by lower profit margins, disappointing hardware revenues and IBM's reported problems with currency translation.
IBM fell 10 points on Wednesday and a further 6-1/4 points on Thursday.
